work: Pappus of Alexandria — Synagoge (Μαθηματικὴ Συναγωγή, ed. Friedrich Hultsch 1876–1878)

units.title: Book III: Problem Hierarchy, Cube Duplication & the Three Classical Means in a Semicircle
Book IV: Generalized Pythagorean Parallelogram Theorem & the Arbelos Tangent Circle Chain
Book V: On the Geometric Forethought of Bees & Honeycomb Isoperimetry
Book VII: The Treasury of Analysis, Centroid Rule, Cross-Ratio & Hexagon Collinearity
Book VIII: Architectonic Mechanics, Centers of Gravity, Five Simple Machines & Seven Hexagons

loci.hultsch_locus: Book III, Chs. 1–27 / Props. 1–5 (Hultsch I, pp. 30–68)
loci.summary: Address to Pandrosion; distinction between theorem and problem; critique of an attempted plane construction of two mean proportionals; canonical classification of plane, solid, and linear problems; cube-duplication solutions of Eratosthenes, Nicomedes, Hero, and Pappus.
euclid_refs: Heath Vol. I, p. 26 (Ch. III, folio 0040)

loci.hultsch_locus: Book III, Chs. 28–43 / Props. 28–30 (Hultsch I, pp. 68–84; esp. p. 72, ll. 9–23)
loci.summary: Definitions of the arithmetic, geometric, and harmonic medieties and Pappus's celebrated semicircle construction exhibiting all three classical means (A, G, H) simultaneously, proving A * H = G^2, A >= G >= H, and external harmonic conjugate T.
euclid_refs: Heath Vol. II, p. 211 (Book VI, Prop. 13 note, folio 0217)

loci.hultsch_locus: Book IV, Ch. 1 / Prop. 1 (Hultsch I, pp. 176–179)
loci.summary: Pappus's Parallelogram Area Theorem: on two sides AB, AC of any triangle ABC erect arbitrary parallelograms ABDE, ACFG whose outer sides meet at H; then the parallelogram BMLC constructed on BC with sides equal and parallel to HA equals ABDE + ACFG — generalizing Elements I.47 and VI.31.
euclid_refs: Heath Vol. I, pp. 366–367 (note on Elements I.47)

loci.hultsch_locus: Book IV, Chs. 19–26 / Props. 14–18 (Hultsch I, pp. 208–232)
loci.summary: The 'ancient proposition' (ἀρχαία πρότασις) on the infinite chain of mutually tangent circles inscribed in the shoemaker's knife (ἄρβηλος): the altitude of the n-th circle's center above the base diameter is an exact integer multiple of its diameter, y_n = n * d_n.

loci.hultsch_locus: Book V, Preface & Props. 1–10 (Hultsch I, pp. 304–336; cf. V.19 pp. 352–358)
loci.summary: Preface to Megethius on the sagacity of bees: why only the equilateral triangle, square, and regular hexagon tile the plane without gaps around a vertex, and why for equal perimeter the regular hexagon encloses maximum honey area (A_6 : A_4 : A_3 = 3*sqrt(3) : 4 : 3), followed by the circle extremum and 13 Archimedean solids.

loci.hultsch_locus: Book VII, Preface & Chs. 1–42 (Hultsch II, pp. 634–688; esp. p. 678 & p. 682)
loci.summary: Preface to Hermodorus on the Treasury of Analysis (τόπος ἀναλυόμενος): theoretical vs. problematic analysis and synthesis, the 33-book canon, Euclid's Porisms, the Three-/Four-Line Locus problem (pp. 676–680), and the Pappus–Guldinus Centroid Rule (p. 682).
euclid_refs: Heath Vol. II, p. 4 (Book III, definitions, folio 0010)
Heath Vol. II, p. 113 (Book V, compound ratio, folio 0119)

loci.hultsch_locus: Book VII, Props. 129, 131, 138–139 (Hultsch II, pp. 868–894; cf. VII.238 pp. 1008–1013)
loci.summary: Lemmas to Euclid's Porisms proving central-perspectivity invariance of the four-point cross-ratio (VII.129), complete-quadrilateral harmonic division (VII.131), and Pappus's Parallel (VII.138) and Intersecting (VII.139) Hexagon Collinearity Theorems.
euclid_refs: Heath Vol. II, p. 27 (Book III, folio 0033)
Heath Vol. II, p. 250 (Book VI, folio 0256)

loci.hultsch_locus: Book VIII, Preface, Props. 1–19 & 23 (Hultsch III, pp. 1022–1102; cf. pp. 1104–1115)
loci.summary: Architectonic mechanics addressed to Hermodorus; center of gravity (p. 1030); inclined-plane equilibrium attempt (Prop. 9, p. 1056); Archimedes's lever saying & Hero's Baroulkos and five simple machines (pp. 1060–1072); single-compass opening constructions (p. 1074); and seven regular hexagons inscribed in a circle of radius R = s_6 * sqrt(7) (Prop. 23, pp. 1096–1102).
